PullRequest.Title: Fix sandbox dependency troubleshooting link
PullRequest.Body:

Updates the sandbox dependency warning's **Troubleshooting Guide** link from the temporary OS-support page to `https://aka.ms/vscode-sandboxing-troubleshoot` and removes the obsolete placeholder comment.

Extends the existing guidance-link test to click the rendered link and assert its exact destination, while preserving coverage for untrusted diagnostic text and trusted command links.

No linked issue.

### Validation

- `npm run build-fast` (VS Code Build Fast task) - passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostSandboxNotification.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 113 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\agentSessions\agentHost\agentHostSandboxNotification.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostSandboxNotification.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `curl.exe -I -L --max-time 30 https://aka.ms/vscode-sandboxing-troubleshoot` - passed; redirects to the VS Code sandbox terminal documentation and returns HTTP 200.

Full type-check, integration tests, and interactive UI testing were not run for this URL-only production change.

Scenarios.Scenario: A sandbox diagnostic appears and the chat input warning is rendered.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A session-state notification calls AgentHostSandboxNotification._update, constructs one short MarkdownString, publishes it, and the active chat notification synchronously parses and inserts that markdown into the DOM. The changed URL is only serialized into the anchor; no network work must complete for rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one deduplicated sandbox-warning notification per session controller for a changed diagnostics/capability state; unchanged state is suppressed by equality checks. The URL length changes by only a constant number of characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates are synchronous per subscription event and the notification service renders the active notification. The diff adds no queue, task, parallel operation, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup or fetch is involved in constructing or rendering the link. Existing notification-state deduplication avoids republishing unchanged diagnostics; cold and warm behavior are equivalent for this URL change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: appendLink only escapes and appends the URL, markdown rendering rewrites it into data-href/href, and no opener call occurs until activation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the changed work is a constant-size string substitution in an already-existing render path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff neither adds synchronous UI work nor increases render frequency, collection size, retained state, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user clicks the warning's Troubleshooting Guide link.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing markdown click listener resolves the anchor and invokes MarkdownRendererService's action handler, which calls IOpenerService.open. One opener operation is required before the external troubleshooting destination can be opened; document loading then occurs outside the notification render path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/markdown/browser/markdownRenderer.ts:84 openLinkFromMarkdown, reached from the changed link at src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSandboxNotification.ts:395
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the external troubleshooting URL through IOpenerService, ultimately allowing the browser/system opener to navigate to documentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener/navigation per user click; no per-item fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same click path issued one opener/navigation to https://aka.ms/ghcp-sandbox-os-support; the diff only substitutes the destination URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only after the user explicitly requests the guide; it is off the warning-render critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One opener/network navigation per explicit user activation, identical to the pre-diff cardinality. Repeated clicks scale linearly exactly as before, with no loop or automatic retry introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-driven activations are not batched or limited by this code, but the diff does not alter their scheduling or concurrency. A normal click triggers one opener call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: VS Code adds no cache or coalescing on this path. Any redirect/document caching belongs to the external opener/browser and is destination-dependent, but the PR does not change application-side cache lifecycle or retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderMarkdown installs click handling, activateLink invokes the action handler only on activation, and MarkdownRendererService delegates exactly once to IOpenerService.open.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Redirect count and remote page latency are external and not established by repository code, but there is no changed in-process multiplicity or scheduling mechanism to support a performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR preserves one user-triggered external open and changes only its target; it does not introduce or amplify boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced notification construction, markdown rendering, click activation, and the opener boundary. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
